prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1359; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim file. I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were and what happened?

A: I was driving on a city street in Pasadena, Texas, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. A car came over into my lane and we hit head-on. It wasn't a violent crash, but the airbag went off and my head snapped forward and back.

Q: Did you have any contact with the other driver after the collision?

A: Briefly. They got out and asked if I was okay. I told them my head hurt and I felt dizzy, and then the police arrived.

Q: Did you receive medical treatment at the scene or afterward?

A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. I was given instructions to rest and avoid screens as much as possible.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Still having headaches most days, and bright lights bother me. I get tired faster than I used to, and I've had trouble concentrating at work. I've been staying home for the past week or so.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the emergency room visit?

A: Yes, I have a follow-up with my primary care physician and I've been referred to a neurologist. I'm keeping a log of my symptoms so I can share it with them.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident or your injuries?

A: Only that I want to make sure my medical bills and lost wages are covered. I'm willing to provide records as needed.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
